battle.name: 靜江之戰
battle.brief: 至元十三年(1276)十一月,元軍自湖廣南下兵臨靜江(今廣西桂林),攻城月餘而城破,守將馬雄力戰被執不屈而死,廣西全境遂平。卡面希臘火本身並未到過這條戰線,但同族技術——猛火油製成的油膏瓶與火藥火砲——正是宋軍城頭與元軍攻城都倚重的燃燒裝備。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 交戰兩方是南宋朝廷的廣西軍政系統與蒙古帝國在廣西的征討軍。南宋一方，靜江府是廣西路的樞紐，府城由知府兼總管馬雄鎮守，府兵由宋廷任命的將校、州縣土官所領的羈縻兵、招募的民兵與弓箭手、隨營匠人組成；糧秣多由桂江上游昭州、潯州方向沿水路運入，城外設有與山城相連的諸寨，寨兵與府兵互為犄角。元一方，兵力屬忽必烈中書省直轄的南方征討序列，由自北南下、業已攻下鄂州潭州的西路大軍推進，蒙古騎兵為骨幹，配漢軍降卒作攻城步卒，並有回回砲手與漢人工匠操作配重式投石機與火藥火砲；廣西各州縣土官多奉文書歸附，個別仍守土城。指揮系統上，元廷以行省與中書省的文書節制遠方軍隊，攻城所需火藥、油膏與攻城器械多自湖廣、江西轉運，沿湘江與桂江分批北送。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Southern Song administrative and military system in Guangxi and the expeditionary force the Mongol Empire brought into the same province. On the Song side, Jingjiang Prefecture was the hinge of the Guangxi circuit. The walled prefectural city was held by the prefect and military commander Ma Xiong, and its garrison was made up of officers appointed by the Song court, the levies of the native tusi chieftains of the neighbouring prefectures and counties, recruited militia and bowmen, and the craftsmen who travelled with the troops. Grain reached the city chiefly by water, brought down the Gui River from Zhao prefecture and Xun prefecture upstream, and a chain of stockades in the hills outside the walls covered the approaches, the stockade fightingmen and the city garrison supporting one another in a mutual system. On the Yuan side the force belonged to the southern campaign commanded directly from the Zhongshu Sheng under the emperor: the western column that had already taken Ezhou, Xiangyang and Tanzhou, advancing south. Mongol cavalry formed its core; Han troops who had surrendered to the Yuan served as assault infantry; and Huihui, or Central Asian, artillerymen together with Han engineers manned counterweight trebuchets and gunpowder bombs. Native chieftains across Guangxi mostly submitted in answer to written summons, though a few still held their own stockade towns. On the command side the Yuan court directed distant armies through the decrees of the provinces and of the central secretariat, and the gunpowder, oil compounds and siege equipment the assault required were shipped in from Huguang and Jiangxi and moved north in batches along the Xiang and Gui rivers.
people: 此役最關鍵的名字是馬雄。他是廣西土著儂人將領，出身行伍，長期任靜江府總管，兼領兵事、兼理民政，是元軍南下時廣西仍在抵抗的中心人物。城陷之日，馬雄力戰不屈，力竭被執，遇害不降；副將與都指揮一級的將校多隨之死守城頭，府兵殘部由城南水門與城外山寨分批退走。另一端的最高指揮者是元世祖忽必烈：至元十三年春，伯顏率軍入臨安，宋廷降服，元廷隨即詔令各路軍掃平殘宋，靜江便在這一輪平定命令之下被圍。攻城技術方面，參與者包括姓名不傳的回回砲手與隨軍工匠，以及搬運、配藥、點火的雜役；宋方則有留城的老將、隨州縣土官調來的援兵指揮與城中的民團首領。關於此役，元代文獻留下的記載相對簡略，具名者只有馬雄一人，其餘多以官軍、民兵、寨兵概稱，難以逐一追蹤各部去向，這也是後人只能從府志、方志與地方傳說中補綴這場戰役的原因。
peopleEn: The decisive name in this campaign is Ma Xiong. He was a Nong native general from Guangxi, a man risen through the ranks, who had long served as military commissioner of Jingjiang Prefecture, holding command of the troops and administrative authority at the same time, and he was the central figure of the resistance that still remained in Guangxi when the Yuan armies came south. On the day the city fell, Ma Xiong fought on without yielding and was taken only when his strength was spent; he was put to death refusing to surrender. Deputy commanders and officers of the rank of regional director defended the walls to the end, while the remnants of the city garrison withdrew in groups through the water gate on the south side and towards the stockades outside the walls. At the other end of the chain of command sat the Yuan emperor Kublai: in the spring of the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era, Bayan marched into Lin'an, the Song court surrendered, and the Yuan court immediately ordered the field armies to sweep up the remaining Song forces. The siege of Jingjiang came directly under that general order. On the technical side the participants included artillerymen from the Huihui whose names were not recorded, the engineers who travelled with the army, and the porters, powder handlers and fire-strikers who served them; on the Song side there were old officers who stayed in the city, commanders of relief detachments sent by the native chieftains, and leaders of the organised militia. The Yuan records for this campaign are comparatively thin. Only Ma Xiong is named; everyone else is covered by such collective terms as the government troops, the militia and the stockade fighters, so the fate of individual units cannot be traced. That is why later writers have had to piece this battle together from local gazetteers and village tradition.
kits: 卡面兵器是希臘火：配在銅管中噴射的燃燒劑，配方為拜占庭帝國的最高機密，配方與相關船隻一同沉沒後再無成方流傳，歐洲中世紀的抄本只留下神話式的描述。它並不會出現在廣西的城頭，這一點必須講清：1276年靜江之戰中，與希臘火同族的是另一支技術——發火油與火藥火砲。宋廷自阿拉伯、波斯商人處取得石油提煉的猛火油，《武經總要》（1044年）已載其收貯與施放之法：灌入厚革囊、油櫃，點燃後拋擲敵陣與樓船，另配硝、硫、炭合成的火藥，投擲式火砲與引信同用。攻守雙方用得上的還有弩與弓，包括南宋神臂弓、蹶張弩這類重射器械，配重式投石機、壕壘用的長槊、雲梯、擲石索，以及沿桂江航行的糧船與載人渡船；馬匹供騎兵機動與搬運火藥、油膏。兵器之外，攻城工程要靠槌、錘、鍬，支撐用的木料與夯土築成的進攻塹壕；守城則靠擂石、滾木、拒馬與城門後的預備突擊隊。
kitsEn: The card shows Greek fire: a burning compound sprayed from a copper tube, its formula the highest secret of the Byzantine Empire, lost together with the craft that carried it, so that no workable recipe survives and the medieval Latin copies preserve only legendary descriptions of it. It never appeared on the walls of Guangxi, and that must be said plainly: what stood beside Greek fire in the fighting at Jingjiang in 1276 was a different branch of the same family of arts, the burning oil and the gunpowder bomb. The Song court obtained petroleum refined into menghuoyou, fierce fire oil, from Arab and Persian merchants, and the Wujing Zongyao of 1044 already records how it was stored and used: it was poured into heavy hide sacks and oil chests, lit, and hurled at enemy formations and tower ships, while gunpowder compounded from saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal was used in thrown bombs fitted with a fuse. Available to both sides were the bow and the crossbow, including heavy-drawing devices such as the Southern Song divine arm bow and the pedal crossbow, together with counterweight trebuchets, long spears for the moat, siege ladders, stone-throwing slings, and the grain boats and ferries that moved on the Gui River. Horses carried cavalry and hauled the gunpowder and the oil compounds. Beyond the arms themselves, siege work demanded hammers, mauls and picks, timber for shoring, and earthen assault trenches; the defence relied on stone-dropping platforms, rolling logs, caltrops and reserve teams stationed behind the gates to counterattack.
tactics: 元軍的攻城套路在十三世紀已經標準化：先以騎兵與漢軍步卒肅清城外，切斷桂江航路與嶺南驛路，封死城內的糧源與援兵，然後以砲隊列陣——配重式投石機壓制城頭、拆除城樓與敵樓，火藥火砲緊接著打擊城門與牆根，同時以工兵從城壕外向內掘地道，木骨撐頂、外覆濕氈，在塌陷處埋設火藥引爆，讓守軍所站立的地面突然崩裂。火攻同時是燃料戰：元軍以油膏、薪柴把城外未及收割的稻田與寨屋燒成焦土，斷絕守軍越冬的接濟。守方則以四門樓櫓為骨幹，分段梯次登城，弓弩在城頭組成封鎖射界，火油瓶與火藥火砲對準接近的雲梯與砲位；每次元軍進至壕溝，守軍即以擂石、滾木、傾潑火油，必要時開門出擊反奪攻城器械。城中守軍多為久戰疲兵，最後的崩解起自糧盡與一段城牆被打穿，而不是一次總攻；守軍選擇了最不利的時機出城反擊，把最後一批能上陣的人手消耗在壕溝外。
tacticsEn: By the thirteenth century the Yuan assault drill was already standardised. Cavalry and Han infantry first cleared the ground outside the walls, cutting the navigation of the Gui River and the roads over the Lingnan passes so that neither grain nor relief could reach the city. Then the artillery line deployed: counterweight trebuchets pressed the parapets and knocked down the gate towers and the fighting platforms, gunpowder bombs followed against the gates and the foot of the wall, and meanwhile engineers dug a tunnel inward from outside the moat, shoring it with timber and covering it with wet felt, packing powder into the cavity and detonating it so that the ground beneath the defenders collapsed without warning. Fire was at the same time a war of fuel: with oil compounds and brush the Yuan burned the unharvested paddy and the stockade houses outside the walls down to a scorched waste, cutting off the garrison's winter supplies. The defence organised itself around the four gate towers and fighting platforms, bringing the defenders up the walls in staged sections, the bows and crossbows of the parapet weaving a interlocking field of fire, and the oil flasks and gunpowder bombs aimed at the siege ladders and artillery positions as they closed. Every time the Yuan reached the moat the garrison dropped stone, rolled logs, poured fire oil, and where it could, opened a gate to counterattack and snatch back the assault equipment. The city troops were for the most part worn down by long service, and their final collapse came from the failure of supplies and from one stretch of wall being broken through, not from a single massed assault; the garrison chose the worst possible moment to sortie and spent the last men it could put on the parapet outside the moat.
data: 可核對的數字不多，以下幾項有據。時間上，至元十三年即公元1276年，十一月起兵、攻城月餘而城破；同年三月伯顏已入臨安，廣西全境於1276至1277年間平定，宋室最後於1279年亡於崖山。城市方面，靜江府城在今廣西桂林，據桂江東岸山地而築，東面臨江為天然險阻，西北依崖修牆，城周約數里，牆高數丈，可擋投石。技術年表可對照：拜占庭希臘火最早可靠的戰場記錄見於678年阿基維魯斯海戰，717至718年君士坦丁堡圍城時仍大量使用，1204年十字軍攻該城時尚見記載，此後配方失傳；中國方面，《武經總要》成書於1044年，已記猛火油與火藥之屬；十二世紀末襄陽攻防的記載出現霹靂火球；1232年蒙古以火藥震天雷破汴京；1267至1273年襄陽之戰中，配重式砲與火藥火砲同時使用，這正是靜江攻城所用器械的直接前身。兵力與傷亡數字，漢文與元代文獻均未留下可信記載，僅稱攻城數月、殺傷甚眾，故此處不列具體人數，只記時序與器物。
dataEn: Few figures about this campaign can be checked, and the following are the ones that hold. On timing: the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era is 1276; the assault began in the eleventh month and the city fell after a siege lasting a little over a month. In the same year, in the third month, Bayan had already entered Lin'an; all of Guangxi was pacified between 1276 and 1277; and the Song house finally ended at Yashan in 1279. On the city: the walled seat of Jingjiang Prefecture stands in what is now Guilin, Guangxi, built along the eastern bank of the Gui River against the hills, with the river forming a natural defence on one side and the wall carried along the cliffs on the other, the circuit measuring several li, the curtain several tens of feet high and strong enough to turn thrown stone. The technical chronology can be set against it. The earliest reliable record of Byzantine Greek fire in battle is the sea battle of Achiropolis in 678; it was used in quantity during the siege of Constantinople in 717 and 718; it was still recorded in use when the Crusaders stormed that city in 1204; and after that the formula was lost. In China, the Wujing Zongyao was completed in 1044 and already describes fierce fire oil and gunpowder; the siege of Xiangyang in the late twelfth century records the thunderbolt fire ball; in 1232 the Mongols broke open Bianjing with gunpowder bombs; and in the siege of Xiangyang from 1267 to 1273 counterweight artillery and gunpowder bombs were used together, the direct ancestor of the equipment used at Jingjiang. For troop strengths and losses the Chinese and Yuan records leave nothing trustworthy, speaking only of a siege lasting months and of heavy killing, so no exact numbers are given here: the chronology and the equipment are what can be set down.
cause: 起戰的根由有兩層。第一層是元廷的滅宋方略：至元十三年春宋廷降於臨安之後，元廷不欲留下任何仍據城池抗元者，詔令各路將帥掃清江南、江西、廣西殘部。靜江扼湘桂走廊北上的咽喉，府城據險，廣西各州縣環衛於外；只要靜江仍在宋軍手中，元朝在嶺南就沒有完整的統治，糧賦與驛傳也無從接管，進取安南的通道也不安全。第二層是廣西內部的權力結構：宋廷以羈縻州安撫當地土官，首領多為世代相傳的儂人、獠人豪族；朝廷既要倚仗他們守邊土，又防其坐大，衝突自唐宋以來一直延續到南宋末年。景炎年間廣西軍政已多制肘，外郡守將屢次不奉調兵之令，援兵不至；元軍所至，州縣土官紛紛奉表城門已下，城中守軍則憑城與糧，獨力抵抗到底。
causeEn: The causes lie on two levels. The first is the Yuan court's strategy for finishing the Song: after the Song court surrendered at Lin'an in the spring of the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era, the court in the north was unwilling to leave any force still holding cities against it, and ordered the commanders on every front to sweep up the remnants in Jiangnan, Jiangxi and Guangxi. Jingjiang commanded the throat of the Xiang-Gui corridor by which an army moves north. Its prefectural city stood on defensible ground, with the other prefectures and counties of Guangxi arrayed around it; as long as Jingjiang stayed in Song hands the Yuan had no complete rule in Lingnan, no regular revenue or courier service, and no safe road to the south towards Annam. The second level lies in the internal structure of power in Guangxi. The Song court governed the native chieftains through the jimi system, and those chieftains were mostly Nong and Liao great families whose office descended through generations. The court needed them to hold the frontier lands while fearing that they would grow too strong, and that tension had run from the Tang and Song down to the end of the Southern Song. Under the Jingyan era the administration of Guangxi had become tangled: commanders in the outer prefectures repeatedly ignored orders to send troops, and relief never came. When the Yuan armies arrived, the native chieftains one after another surrendered and opened their gates, while the garrison inside the city, with nothing but the walls and what grain they could hold, resisted to the end.
impact: 靜江陷落標誌著南宋在廣西的抵抗力量被清剿殆盡，嶺南再無成建制的宋軍政力量，元朝自此取得廣西的稅源、驛路與對安南用兵的通道，次年便可把兵鋒指向廣東沿海與海上。治理上，元廷在廣西仍大量倚重土官，但把靜江府降為路、置總管府，並以宣慰司與行省民政逐步收編州縣，形成土官與流官混處的格局，此後數百年廣西的行政框架由此奠定。軍事技術上，此役是火藥兵器在南方山城的一次完整演練：配重砲打擊城樓、火藥砲破門、地道爆破配合騎兵封鎖，三種手段同時出現於一場城池攻防，說明攻城戰已從攀登與破門，轉向以火藥與機械主導的工程戰；而火油這類流動燃燒劑在城頭的拋擲與傾潑，亦顯示燃燒技術已從水軍火船，擴散到內陸山城守城。這套經驗在宋元最後的海上決戰與更遠的海外征伐中繼續被使用，也為後來的中原王朝留下了攻城器械與火藥配合的範式。
impactEn: The fall of Jingjiang marked the destruction of the Southern Song's power of resistance in Guangxi. No formed Song military or political force remained in Lingnan, and the Yuan court gained Guangxi's revenue, its courier roads and the route for operating against Annam; the year after, its arms could be turned towards the coast of Guangdong and out to sea. In the sphere of government, the Yuan continued to lean heavily on the native chieftains in Guangxi, but reduced Jingjiang Prefecture to a circuit with a military commission, and gradually took the prefectures and counties into the hands of pacification commissions and provincial civil administration, producing a mixed order in which hereditary tusi and appointed officials governed side by side; the administrative framework of Guangxi for the centuries to come was set here. In military technology the campaign was a complete demonstration of gunpowder weapons before a southern hill city: counterweight artillery striking the gate towers, gunpowder bombs against the gates, and mine explosions coordinated with cavalry sealing the approaches. All three methods appeared in a single siege, showing that siege warfare had moved away from scaling and battering and towards engineering dominated by powder and machinery. The hurling and pouring of oil compounds along the parapet likewise showed that the burning technique had spread from the fire ship of the fleets to the defence of inland hill towns. This experience was carried on into the last naval battles of the Song and Yuan and into more distant overseas expeditions, and it left the Yuan and later Chinese dynasties a model in which siege engines and gunpowder worked together.
result: 城破之日，靜江落入元軍之手，馬雄被執不屈而死，守城將校多死於城頭，餘部由水路與城外山寨分散退往廣東。廣西各州縣在隨後一兩年內陸續歸附：柳州、慶遠、邕州等地或降或下，至此嶺南再無對抗元廷的成建制軍隊，宋室的殘餘朝廷退守海上，兩年後在崖山覆滅。從戰役本身看，結果是明確的：蒙古軍以封鎖、砲擊與地道爆破的組合，攻破了被認為不可輕取的西南山城；代價則是攻城月餘、耗費大量火藥、油膏與投石機，並未能阻止零星山寨以持久抗擊的形式延續數年。這場戰役在宋元史中常被視為元軍平定廣西的收尾之役，也是帝國在華南完成軍事統一的一個節點；對後人而言，它更記錄了火藥兵器與配重砲首次在南方城防中正面發揮作用的一個樣本，其慘烈與其成功都成為下一個時代攻城戰的教科書。
resultEn: On the day the city fell, Jingjiang passed into the hands of the Yuan army. Ma Xiong was taken and died refusing to yield; most of the officers who had defended the walls died on them; the remnants of the garrison scattered towards Guangdong by water and through the stockades outside the city. The other prefectures and counties of Guangxi submitted over the following year or two: Liuzhou, Qingyuan and Yongzhou surrendered or were taken, and from that moment no formed military force in Lingnan stood against the Yuan court, while the remnant Song court withdrew to the sea and was destroyed at Yashan two years later. Judged as a campaign, the outcome is plain. The Mongol army broke a south-western hill city that had been considered impregnable, combining blockade, artillery and mined tunnels; the price was a siege of a little over a month, a great expenditure of gunpowder, oil compounds and trebuchets, and the failure to stop scattered stockades from carrying on a stubborn resistance for years afterwards. In the histories of Song and Yuan this campaign is usually treated as the closing stage of the pacification of Guangxi and as a milestone in the empire's military unification of South China. To later readers it is also the record of a single case in which gunpowder weapons and counterweight artillery first told decisively in the defence of a southern city, its cost and its success alike becoming a textbook for the siege warfare of the age that followed.
